thread.title: Charting the S&P 500’s bullish spike atop the 20-day volatility bands

author: Michael Ashbaugh
title: Charting the S&P 500’s bullish spike atop the 20-day volatility bands
text:
Editor’s Note: This is a free edition of The Technical Indicator, a daily MarketWatch subscriber newsletter. To get this column each market day, click here.
Several widely-tracked U.S. benchmarks have staged statistically unusual June breakouts, strengthening an already-bullish technical backdrop ahead of the Federal Reserve’s expected mid-week interest-rate hike.
Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 has extended its June rally — edging atop the 2,780 resistance — while the Nasdaq Composite is concurrently vying for its latest record close.
Before detailing the U.S. markets’ wider view, the S&P 500’s SPX, +0.15% hourly chart highlights the past two weeks.
As illustrated, the S&P has extended the June breakout.
Tactically, the 2,780 area remains an inflection point, matching consecutive session highs and Monday’s session low. Delving deeper, a firmer floor matches the May peak (2,742).
Similarly, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has broken out.
In its case, an inflection point rests at 25,326, closely matching consecutive session highs, and Monday’s close (25,322).
Conversely, the May peak (25,086) marks near-term support and is followed by a significant floor matching the 2017 peak (24,876).
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite has pulled in modestly from record territory.
Tactically, the breakout point (7,637) matches the March peak, and is closely followed by an inflection point just under the 7,600 mark. Conversely, the Nasdaq’s record high (7,697) is once again under siege early Tuesday.
Widening the view to six months, the Nasdaq’s daily chart includes its 20-day Bollinger bands, also known as volatility bands. Illustrated in red, the bands encompass two standard deviations of the Nasdaq’s trailing 20-day volatility.
Consider that consecutive closes atop the bands signal a tension between two time horizons.
For the near-term, the index is overbought, and due to consolidate. The breakout has been statistically unusual, placing it outside the trailing two standard deviation range.
But more importantly, the underlying bullish momentum has registered as extreme, and likely lays the groundwork for longer-term upside follow-through.
The Nasdaq’s initial June breakout encompassed four consecutive closes atop the bands, the month’s first four sessions. Distinctly bullish price action.
By comparison, the subsequent pullback has been flat — illustrated on the hourly chart — likely positioning the index for incremental follow-through.
Looking elsewhere, the Dow Jones Industrial Average has extended its June breakout.
The blue-chip benchmark is playing catch up, after lagging behind until last Wednesday.
More broadly, the Dow is rising from a modified double bottom defined by the March and May lows. An intermediate-term target projects to the 26,200 area, initially detailed last week.
(Start with the April peak and subtract the May low: 24,859 - 23,531 = 1,328 points. Then, add back to the breakout point: 24,859 + 1,328 = 26,187.)
(Recall that the March closing low (23,533) matched the absolute May low (23,531).)
Like the Nasdaq, the S&P 500 has staged a two standard deviation breakout.
In its case, the S&P has notched three straight closes atop the volatility bands, a stretch that was snapped Monday. The June rally has stalled, at least temporarily, near the 2,780 inflection point, detailed previously.
The bigger picture Collectively, an already-bullish June backdrop continues to strengthen.
On a headline basis, the Nasdaq Composite has reached uncharted territory, a move punctuated by four consecutive closes atop the 20-day volatility bands.
Meanwhile, the S&P 500 and Dow industrials have staged less decisive breakouts, though each still registers as statistically unusual. The S&P 500 has recently notched three consecutive closes atop the volatility bands, while the Dow’s breakout initially encompassed two straight closes atop the bands.
As always, consecutive closes atop the bands are statistically unusual, and longer-term distinctly bullish.
Moving to the small-caps, the iShares Russell 2000 ETF is digesting the June breakout amid flat selling pressure.
The prevailing rally originates from the breakout point (160.00).
Meanwhile, the S&P MidCap 400’s slow-motion break to record territory remains underway.
Tactically, the breakout point (362.50) pivots to well-defined support.
Against this backdrop, the SPDR Trust S&P 500 has tagged nearly three-month highs, its best level since March 13.
More distant inflection points match the February peak (278.92) and March peak (280.41).
Summing up the backdrop All told, the U.S. benchmarks acting well technically after the U.S.-North Korea meeting and ahead of an expected mid-week Federal Reserve interest-rate hike.
Placing a finer point on the S&P 500, its recent price action registers as firmly bullish.
The index started June with a bull-flag breakout, clearing the May peak. The prevailing upturn originates from major support matching the trendline and the 2017 close (2,673).
Morover, the June rally has registered as statistically unusual, encompassing a two standard deviation breakout.
Tactically, the 2,780 area remains a near-term inflection point.
On further strength, additional overhead matches the March peak (2,802) while an intermediate-term target continues to project to the 2,811 area.
See also: Charting a jagged June breakout attempt, Nasdaq challenges record territory.
Tuesday’s Watch List The charts below detail names that are technically well positioned. These are radar screen names — sectors or stocks poised to move in the near term. For the original comments on the stocks below, see The Technical Indicator Library.
Drilling down further, the transports have belatedly broken out.
As illustrated, the iShares Transportation Average ETF IYT, +0.47% has reached four-month highs, rising from a bull flag — the tight two-week range — pinned to the early-May rally.
The prevailing upturn originates from trendline support, as well as a successful test of the 200-day moving average.
More immediately, the group is traversing less-charted territory, and an intermediate-term target closely matches its record high at the January peak. An eventual retest looks increasingly likely.
Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF KRE, -0.60% is acting well ahead of the Fed’s expected interest-rate hike, due out Wednesday.
The group benefits from rising interest rates in the form of an improved rate spread, or the difference between the rates at which a bank borrows and subsequently lends to its customers.
Technically, the group has reached record territory, rising from a cup-and-handle pattern defined by the April and May lows. Trendline support underpins the pattern.
Tactically, the breakout point (65.00) is closely followed by the trendline, circa 63, and the group’s path of least resistance points higher barring a violation.
Public since September 2017, Roku, Inc. ROKU, +0.58% is a mid-cap streaming video platform operator.
As illustrated, the shares have rallied to three-month highs, on increased volume, clearing resistance matching the March breakdown point.
Underlying the upturn, its relative strength index (not illustrated) has notched a year-to-date peak, improving the chances of incremental follow-through. Tactically, the former range top (40.00) matches well-defined support, and Roku’s recovery attempt is intact barring a violation.
Microchip Technology, Inc. MCHP, +0.40% is a well positioned large-cap semiconductor name.
Earlier this month, the shares rallied to all-time highs, clearing resistance matching the March peak.
The ensuing pullback has been flat, underpinned by the breakout point, positioning the shares to extend the June rally. Tactically, a near-term floor matches the post-breakout low (100.80) and a posture higher supports a bullish bias.
Analog Devices, Inc. ADI, +0.20% is a large-cap semiconductor name positioned to rise.
Late last month, the shares cleared trendline resistance, extending to 17-year highs after the company’s second-quarter results.
Though still near-term extended, the nearly straightline June spike is longer-term bullish, and the shares are attractive on a pullback. The post-breakout low (100.00) is followed by a firmer floor matching the breakout point (97.90).
Viking Therapeutics, Inc. VKTX, -1.13% is a well positioned speculative small-cap biotech name.
As illustrated, the shares have recently knifed to record territory, rising in sympathy with positive Phase 2 study results for Madrigal Pharmaceuticals’ steatohepatitis treatment. Viking’s developmental drug has a similar treatment mechanism.
By comparison, the ensuing pullback has been flat, and punctuated by Monday’s record close. Tactically, the May closing peak has marked an inflection point (9.99, a level capping the long white bar) and the rally attempt is intact barring a violation.
